value.title: UV scalar product additivity and symmetry
value.objective: Determine the tensorization and blocking behavior of separately relaxed UV sum-rate scalar functionals, including symmetry conditions that identify their branchwise and averaged forms.
value.currentStateSummary: The averaged separately relaxed UV scalar is exactly additive for arbitrary finite-alphabet DMBC products, even with correlated product-channel inputs and joint envelope auxiliaries. Receiver-skew symmetry equates the branchwise and averaged scalars and is preserved by finite products. Consequently, every finite power of the half-skew BSSC has normalized value 2h2(1/4)-5/4, which is weaker than the certified capacity upper bound and does not change the capacity frontier.
value.localResidualSummary: Determine whether any stronger coupled UV formulation, complete UV region, other weighted scalarization, nested auxiliary construction, or full Theorem-9 system tensorizes or can yield a sharper BSSC converse; the established theorem does not cover those objectives.

value.title: Exact UV product and receiver-skew branchwise additivity
value.statement: For a finite-alphabet DMBC W, let t_W(p)=I_p(X;Y)-I_p(X;Z), let C denote the upper concave envelope on the input simplex, and define A_W(p)=I_p(X;Y)+C[-t_W](p), D_W(p)=I_p(X;Z)+C[t_W](p), B_avg(W)=sup_p (A_W(p)+D_W(p))/2, and B_br(W)=sup_p min{A_W(p),D_W(p)}. Then B_avg(W1×W2)=B_avg(W1)+B_avg(W2) for arbitrary finite-alphabet DMBCs, including correlated product-channel priors and envelope auxiliaries joint across factors. If an involutive input relabeling exchanges the receivers, then B_br(W)=B_avg(W), and the optimization may be restricted to invariant input laws. Finite products preserve this symmetry, so both functionals are exactly additive on arbitrary finite products of receiver-skew-symmetric channels. For the half-skew BSSC P, the invariant binary prior is fair and, using the accepted sharp BSSC posterior support, B_br(P^{×n})=B_avg(P^{×n})=n(2h2(1/4)-5/4) for every finite n≥1, with normalized value 0.3725562489182657… bits per channel use.
scopeQualifications: The theorem concerns the two separately relaxed UV sum-rate rows and their averaged or pointwise-minimum scalarizations; it does not establish tensorization of the complete UV rate region or simultaneous attainment by a common joint (U,V) law.
Branchwise equality is established under receiver-skew symmetry and is not claimed for nonsymmetric channels or other weighted UV scalarizations.
The theorem does not tensorize the simplified GK functional, nested auxiliary-receiver constructions, or the full Gohari–Liu–Nair Theorem-9 constraint system.

The half-skew BSSC value is a valid non-frontier converse value. It exceeds the certified full-Theorem-9 upper bound 0.369296945969202842443 and therefore changes neither endpoint of the governed capacity interval.
No achievability result or capacity formula follows.

proofs: For a product DMBC and an arbitrary auxiliary A, a forward/reverse chain-rule expansion gives an exact cancellation of the cross co-information terms at coefficient one. The conditioned variables remaining in the two summands are valid one-factor auxiliaries, yielding factorwise upper bounds for both concave envelopes even under correlated inputs.

Mutual-information subadditivity and the envelope inequalities give the product upper bound for B_avg. Product priors together with independent near-optimal posterior decompositions give the reverse inequality and hence exact additivity.

Under the receiver-skew involution S, t(Sp)=-t(p), the envelope decompositions are carried bijectively to one another, and A_W(Sp)=D_W(p). Concavity at the invariant symmetrization (p+Sp)/2 proves B_br≥B_avg, while min(a,d)≤(a+d)/2 proves the reverse inequality.

The coordinatewise receiver-skew involution makes every finite product receiver-skew-symmetric. Combining symmetry equality with averaged-functional additivity proves finite-product additivity of both scalar functionals.

For the half-skew BSSC, the sharp posterior-support inequality and its reflected form identify the fair-prior envelope contact. The source mixture supported at posterior parameters 0 and 4/5 attains the contact, giving the exact one-letter value 2h2(1/4)-5/4.
methods: Exact chain-rule factorization for product broadcast channels, upper-concave-envelope decomposition, mutual-information subadditivity, product posterior mixtures, involutive receiver-exchange covariance, and concavity-based symmetrization.
Dependency-ordered specialization using the sharp BSSC posterior support represented by ir-code-induced-balance-entropy-nogo.

Analytic proofs are retained in source-artifacts/upper-uv-additivity/FULL.md (SHA-256 69a33f9fc84a5dbabbad6bdf53b34e722238c6a6b3f625d49e00f599e942b94a) and source-artifacts/frontier-uv-branchwise/FULL.md (SHA-256 64ddb2c3d0c375bbca746842e21689f11883d989d56a0f0028ceaf216715e623).
computations: The BSSC specialization evaluates exactly to 2h2(1/4)-5/4=0.3725562489182657… bits per channel use; finite powers multiply this value by the blocklength.
The normalized UV value 0.3725562489182657… is numerically larger, and hence weaker as an upper bound, than the certified full-Theorem-9 value 0.369296945969202842443.
A 90-digit Decimal audit checks the BSSC envelope contact, fair-prior barycenter, receiver-skew matrices, and exact-form numerical evaluation.
tools: Python 3 standard-library audit source-artifacts/upper-uv-additivity/verify_uv_factorization.py (SHA-256 bdd966d11f1914425ed4932b459c83508a6a61a73131f4f2a184204ad0c4153e) checks the product chain identities, conditional Markov relations, mutual-information subadditivity, product mixtures, and BSSC contact value.

Python 3 hostile-case audit verify_uv_hostile_cases.py (SHA-256 ffa2b5d66670f0fd03338e73f8ecc5400bf23b162a92fa327f363c7bb1aac6c0) checks deterministic and zero-probability channels, correlated and degenerate inputs, receiver-skew matrices, and the high-precision BSSC specialization.

placementAudit.rationale: The accepted theorem chain advances one durable objective—tensorization and symmetry of separately relaxed UV scalar converses—distinct from the existing code-induced converse-structure program. Its BSSC specialization depends on the prior posterior-support result without changing that prior program's objective or result ownership.

topologyRationale: Create a new active sibling program under the canonical root and place the single reusable dependency-ordered theorem chain in it. No existing program or result is moved, retired, split, merged, or reassigned.
